title: CAR-005 Route Resolution Report
description: The report one resolution walk produces, and the single shape every corpus case pins. ONE shape discriminated by the required outcome field, never a root-level oneOf and never two report documents (FR-013a): the FR-024 override path emits a no_safe_route report that still carries effective_dispatch_tuple, so a success variant and a failure variant do not partition the field space. Conditional requiredness is therefore expressed as allOf + if/then branches carrying required and not: {required: [...]}, the idiom the committed Layer 6 Claude contracts already use. No $ref leaves this document's own #/$defs/ (FR-016).

agent.description: The reported subject's name — the policy's root agent. One report per policy, so this stays single-valued even when the policy also declares an optional helper, which is what keeps outcome, unresolved_agent, and effective_dispatch_tuple single-valued too.

outcome.description: FR-013a: the discriminator, closed at two members. An override never promotes it to resolved (FR-024a), which is why the override branch below is independent of the outcome branches rather than exclusive with them.

attempted_routes.description: FR-004: array order IS attempt order, so there is no redundant index field. minItems 0 because a pre-walk structural rejection records no attempts and must have a valid representation — the array is empty if and only if the pre-walk pass rejected the policy (FR-019c). This is a deliberate departure from the directory's one existing attempt-array precedent, contracts/treatment-record.schema.json, which declares attempted_route_ids with minItems 1; FR-019c's biconditional replaces the guarantee that bound was providing.

diagnostics.description: Present, possibly empty: FR-011's clean success emits none, so no minItems is declared. Order is the three-stage sequence FR-012b fixes — pre-walk policy violations, then per-route entries in attempt order, then unqualified_override, then exactly one terminal no_safe_route entry last. FR-016a: the two closed vocabularies are declared as two diagnostic-entry $defs, each carrying its own inline code enum, and unioned HERE by oneOf rather than as bare-enum $defs members — no bare-enum $defs exists anywhere in this contracts directory. The two enums are disjoint, so exactly one branch matches any conforming entry.

release_claim_eligible.description: FR-024a: true only as a residual. It is false under an override, under no_safe_route, or with any policy-violation diagnostic present. This is the dedicated gate field, which is why severity stays descriptive rather than becoming the gate.

optional_helper.description: FR-025: structured, never a diagnostic. Neither closed enum gains a member for helper unavailability.

effective_dispatch_tuple.description: FR-013: what resolution selected, so a consumer reads the outcome without re-deriving it from the attempt list. Conditional — see the allOf branches.

unresolved_agent.description: FR-019c: the policy's own agent name. Conditional — see the allOf branches.

override.description: Optional, present only when the synthetic environment carries one.

allOf.description: FR-013a branch 1: a resolved walk names the tuple it selected and cannot also name an unresolved agent.
FR-013a branch 2: a walk that resolved nothing names the agent left unresolved.

FR-013a branch 3, and what makes the override path expressible: combined with branch 2 it yields a no_safe_route report carrying BOTH unresolved_agent and effective_dispatch_tuple, which is precisely the field combination a root oneOf could not express. Note what it does not do: it does not make the report resolved.

resolutionDiagnostic.description: FR-005 and FR-012: one rejection or terminal entry, in the installed runner's diagnostics envelope shape. code, message, severity, source, and remediation are REQUIRED and details is optional, mirroring the runner, which always emits the first five (substituting default remediation when the caller passes none) and emits details only when non-empty. Note the trap this deliberately avoids: a different diagnostics dialect exists elsewhere in the tree — an autopilot gate-state contract that requires details and omits remediation, the inverse of the runner — and it is NOT the precedent. remediation is a field of each diagnostic entry and never a top-level report field; hoisting it would create the second dialect FR-012 forbids.

code.description: FR-005 and FR-017a: exactly, and verbatim, the five codes the Claude routing roadmap pins. This pointer — $defs/resolutionDiagnostic/properties/code/enum — is FR-017a's live read target, and nothing else may restate these five members anywhere. The third member is a recorded, permanent, intentional platform divergence: Codex pins capability_discovery_unavailable, because Codex treats discovery and probing as distinct concepts while Claude has no such split (FR-017b, FR-017c).

message.description: maxLength 240 because the installed runner truncates there.

severity.description: FR-012c: closed to the runner's own three values, but the VALUE is a function of code rather than of the occurrence — the four route-rejection codes are warning, because a rejected route is not itself a failure while the walk may still resolve on a later fallback, and no_safe_route is error. This is a deliberate divergence from the runner, whose severity is caller-determined; it is justified because this feature's emitter is a hand-authored, byte-compared corpus, where leaving severity to the emitter would be unfalsifiable authoring latitude. info is declared by the closed vocabulary and emitted by no code.

source.description: FR-012c: one literal per producing module, mirroring the runner, which hardcodes exactly that and keys its own is_diagnostic predicate off the value. Left as an open string it would be an unpinned byte in every diagnostic of every case. Capability-named, never spec-ID-named (FR-032).

details.description: The one deliberately OPEN object in this document (additionalProperties true), mirroring the runner's dict[str, Any]. Openness is load bearing, not laziness: slice 2 must add no schema field, so details must already admit every payload slice 2 emits. The named properties are pinned in slice 1 and are exactly those the resolution codes carry, per the carried-by mapping in data-model.md section 3; case-specific values live here and are never interpolated into a remediation action string.

sub_reason.description: FR-006: the closed four-member set, total over the projection and evaluated in THIS order so exactly one member applies to any snapshot and replay stays byte-identical. Their exclusivity is not uniform, which is why the order is structural rather than decorative: the first three partition the state of alias_bindings against available_models and cannot co-occur, while platform_route_changed reads the separate platform_route_changes array and so CAN co-occur with any of the first three — it is disjoint only because it is evaluated last.

route_id.description: FR-029a: the join key back to the matching attempted_routes entry, carried by every route-scoped diagnostic.

exhausted_budget.description: FR-026a: carried by the terminal no_safe_route diagnostic only, listing every budget class whose actual count equals its declared cap, in enum declaration order. This is how a consumer tells WHICH budget exhausted.

allOf.description: FR-006 and FR-029a: the sub-reason payload plus the join key. Each branch requires BOTH details and route_id within it, since a join key living in an optional object — or in a required object as an optional member — is not a key a consumer can rely on.
FR-007 and FR-029a: naming both the declared effort and the model's supported efforts, plus the join key.

policyViolationDiagnostic.description: FR-019: the second closed vocabulary, identical envelope. Declared in SLICE 1 alongside the resolution enum even though no slice-1 corpus case can emit one. Declaring a closed vocabulary in full while most members are unexercised is the established practice in this directory, not a review smell — score-bundle.schema.json declares a 12-member and a 36-member enum of which at most four members are exercised by any shipped fixture — and it means slice 2 modifies no schema file at all, strictly stronger than append-only additivity. It is not a separate document: cross-document $ref resolution is prohibited here, so a separate document could only be referenced illegally, and it would force the enum to be restated — the exact drift the read-enums-live discipline exists to prevent.

code.description: FR-019 and FR-019b: exactly these five members, read live by JSON pointer for the set-equality assertion. The Codex roadmap's rejection list is strictly longer, but those additions have no Claude analogue and importing them would be enum drift, not parity.

severity.description: FR-012c: the four policy-authoring violations are error, because they mark a policy that is unusable as written. unqualified_override is warning because dispatch proceeds under it — its consequence is carried by release_claim_eligible false, not by the severity, and that holds even when it coexists with no_safe_route.

details.description: Open on the same terms as the resolution diagnostic's details. route_id is the one named property, because it is the one member of the details vocabulary that a policy-violation code carries (FR-029a); naming it is what gives the join key a type rather than leaving it any JSON value the open object would otherwise admit.

allOf.description: FR-020 and FR-029a. Without these four branches, four of the eight route-scoped codes could validly omit details and so omit the route key — the join would hold for resolution rejections and silently fail for policy-authoring ones, which is the half-covered state a reviewer would be least likely to notice.
FR-023 and FR-029a. unqualified_override takes NO branch, and that is the deliberate exception: it is an environment condition scoped to no route (FR-019c), so it has no route_id to carry.

remediation.description: FR-012a: the remediation each diagnostic entry carries. Both bounds mirror the installed runner, which truncates the action list with actions[:3] and substitutes a default so the list is never empty — a fourth action would be silently discarded by the real runner. DOCUMENTED DEVIATION: FR-012a's earlier wording named this vocabulary $defs.remediationAction. It is instead declared inline at $defs/remediation/properties/actions/items/enum, because FR-016a prohibits bare-enum $defs members and this directory has ZERO of them across all eleven documents — a $defs.remediationAction holding a top-level enum would be the first, breaking the very invariant FR-016a cites. Inlining preserves everything FR-012a asks for in substance: one closed set, literal strings, a single declaration site in this document, and a stable JSON pointer for a set-equality test. Only the $defs name is given up. Recorded in plan.md Complexity Tracking.

actions.description: A closed inline enum of LITERAL strings — no structured objects and no templates with substitution slots. Structured entries would be the second dialect FR-012 forbids, since the runner types this field as a list of plain strings; templates would degrade closure from set equality to one regex per template. Case-specific values (the missing model ID, the declared and supported efforts, the observed alias binding) live in the diagnostic's details object, so a consumer acts on set membership without parsing prose. Eleven members: one apt action per code across both closed vocabularies, plus the mandated rollback. 'Roll back to the previous plugin release.' is verbatim per FR-012a and FR-029, the imperative rendering of the roadmap's own guidance, and the no_safe_route diagnostic's actions must include it. The per-code allocation is recorded in data-model.md section 3: the mapping is one-to-one except for no_safe_route, which is the only code carrying both a forward remedy and the rollback, so the maximum is 2 against a cap of 3 and no code is near the truncation boundary.

enum: Roll back to the previous plugin release.
Widen the declared fallback list with qualified routes.
Re-probe the environment and confirm the pinned alias and resolved model.
Declare an effort the model's probed capability set supports.
Re-run capability probing before trusting this route.
Inspect the exact-invocation probe evidence for this route.
Remove the repeated route from the fallback chain.
Replace the adjacent model with a qualified route.
Restore the named agent in the fallback route.
Declare the model and effort explicitly on the route.
Unset the unqualified subagent-model override before making release claims.

attemptedRoute.description: One entry of the attempt-ordered list. Model and effort stay optional here for the same reason as in the route policy: an inherit-materialization route must be recordable as attempted (FR-023).

dispatchTuple.description: FR-013: all four members required. On the honored override branch this tuple is a HYBRID rather than a copy of the override — the environment variable sets a model only, so alias and resolved_model come from the override's requested value while agent and effort are retained from the route the qualified walk selected, or from the preferred route when it selected none. Attributing each member is what makes the pinned bytes derivable rather than implementation-defined.

reportedBudgets.description: FR-026: the declared caps alongside the actual counts, so 'never exceeds the declared budget' is checkable from the report alone. Each actual counter's unit is fixed by FR-026a: probe_attempts once per route's FIRST probe-state consultation, reading capability-probe availability and the exact-invocation outcome together as one consultation; retries once per consultation of a route after its first, which is what makes retry exhaustion reachable against a static snapshot; candidate_routes once per candidate route entered, so it equals the length of attempted_routes whenever the walk runs. Hence probe_attempts <= candidate_routes always, and the two are not redundant — a route rejected before probing is reached raises candidate_routes without raising probe_attempts. The declared caps carry the same bounds as the policy's declaredBudgets, so a report cannot echo a cap the policy could never have declared.

optionalHelper.description: FR-025a: all three members required, in all three helper states. probe_attempts is DISJOINT from budgets.actual.probe_attempts — the former counts probes spent on the helper's declared routes, the latter the reported agent's own walk. The counter exists so that 'not consulted' is a measurable zero rather than a self-asserted boolean: an implementation could otherwise probe every helper route and still write consulted false without changing a pinned byte.

override.description: FR-024 and FR-024b: the unqualified subagent-model override in force. Four of its members exist because of FR-024b's fidelity rules. source is const to the documented environment variable's name, for the same reason the diagnostic source is const: a required field left as an open string is an unpinned byte in every case that carries it, and an override whose mechanism is anonymous cannot be checked against a documented behaviour at all. requested_model is the raw override value, which the documentation permits to be either a family alias or a full model ID, and is recorded separately from tuple because the two differ on the skipped branch. qualified is a separate boolean from the allowlist disposition because the two gates are independent: an override can be unqualified yet allowlist-permitted, or qualified yet allowlist-excluded. release_claim_eligible is false on either branch and for either value, since any override in force excludes the environment.

disposition.description: The two documented outcomes. honored is the branch where the target passes the organization allowlist and the override becomes the effective dispatch tuple; skipped_by_allowlist is the branch where the platform skips a value resolving to an excluded model.

would_have_been.description: FR-024a: the would-have-been qualified resolution. Its own outcome member is what makes the spec's edge case expressible — an unqualified override present AND no qualified route resolving still records the override as effective, still sets release_claim_eligible false, and still reports the would-have-been outcome as no_safe_route. In that case effective_dispatch_tuple is OMITTED, never present as null, because canonical serialization renders both forms deterministically and omission is what the rest of this report already does for conditional members.

allOf.description: FR-024b: the honored branch names the hybrid tuple that actually dispatches.

FR-024b: tuple is FORBIDDEN on the skipped branch. The runtime's documented fallback target there is the INHERITED model, which this projection does not carry, so recording any tuple would be asserting a model the simulation cannot know.
